Package index

Run the pipeline

One call does everything. The stage functions below are the same code, split so a step can be run, inspected or replaced on its own.

run_cyraven()
run_cyraven

Reading and transformation

Getting FCS files into a matrix on a sensible scale. The transform is selectable, and its parameters are derived once per panel so every sample stays on one ruler.

read_fcs_resolved()
Read one FCS file and resolve marker symbols
fingerprint_panels()
Group files into panels by their exact marker set
maybe_compensate()
Apply the spillover matrix if one is present WHY: spectral instruments (e.g. Sony ID7000) write already-unmixed data and carry no $SPILLOVER keyword. Compensating twice, or erroring because the matrix is absent, are both wrong – detect and report.
make_transform()
Build the intensity transform the whole run uses
derive_cofactor()
Derive the arcsinh cofactor from the data
derive_cofactor_pooled()
Derive the panel cofactor from SEVERAL samples, not from whichever file was read first
derive_logicle_pooled()
Derive one set of transform parameters for a panel

Gating

Thresholds derived from each sample’s own density rather than transferred from fixed coordinates.

density_valley()
Find the deepest density valley between two modes
resolve_threshold()
Resolve a threshold for one marker, recording where the value came from
apply_gate_hierarchy()
Apply the full gate hierarchy to one file
staining_verdict()
Staining QC verdict per file

Uncertainty

How far a threshold can move, and what that costs the frequency it produced. Each cut is resampled and re-derived over the settings that placed it, and the resulting spread is propagated to every population that reads it. None of this changes a reported number; it puts a second number beside it.

threshold_uncertainty()
Uncertainty in one per-sample threshold
population_frequency_uncertainty()
Propagate threshold uncertainty into one sample's population frequencies
run_gate_uncertainty()
Run the whole uncertainty analysis over a scored cohort
annotate_gate_uncertainty()
Compare a between-group difference against the gate uncertainty behind it
valley_setting_grid()
The settings sweep that produces the method component

Populations

Scoring a declarative population specification.

score_populations()
Evaluate the population spec against one file's thresholded markers
default_population_spec()
Built-in population spec, derived from the supplied gating strategy
default_functional_blocks()
Functional marker blocks, transcribed from the document's four scoping rules
expected_positive_markers()
Markers each population's gate definition requires to be POSITIVE
compute_population_ratios()
Derived abundance ratios (e.g. CD4:CD8), from the config's ratios: block

Embedding

One shared UMAP per marker panel, plus model persistence for later batches.

select_umap_features()
Choose the markers that define the embedding space
plan_subsample()
Draw a size-balanced subsample of gated cells across samples
run_umap()
Build the UMAP input matrix and run the embedding
save_umap_model()
Save a trained UMAP model plus the scaling needed to reproduce its input
load_umap_model()
Load a saved UMAP model
project_umap()
Project new cells into a saved embedding

Clustering

Unsupervised clustering as a cross-check on the gate specification, and reference-defined subclustering.

run_unsupervised_clusters()
Unsupervised clustering of the embedded cells
cluster_gate_agreement()
Cross-tabulate unsupervised clusters against gate labels
subcluster_by_reference()
Split each cluster into subclusters DEFINED ON THE REFERENCE GROUP
choose_subcluster_k()
Choose k per population from the reference group's cells

Learned gates

The inverse of the gating stage: given a set of labelled cells, learn a two-marker gating strategy that selects them. This is what turns “this cluster matches no described population” into a gate someone can draw. Descriptive throughout – it proposes gates and never changes a scored one.

learn_convex_gate()
Learn a convex two-marker gate for a labelled set of cells
explain_cluster()
Learn a hierarchical gating strategy for one labelled population
explain_unmatched_clusters()
Propose gating strategies for clusters the spec does not describe
rank_gate_markers()
Rank markers by how differently they are distributed in targets and the rest
fig_gate_strategy()
Draw a proposed gating strategy, one panel per gate

Labels from another tool

Take a cell labelling this package did not produce, a cyCONDOR clustering for instance, learn a gate that selects it, and find out whether that gate holds on a donor it was not fitted to. Held-out cells come from the same donors as the training cells and overstate transferability; refitting with one donor withheld does not.

read_external_labels()
Read cell labels produced by another tool
join_external_labels()
Attach external labels to the embedding cell table
explain_external_labels()
Learn and validate a gate for each externally supplied label
gate_transferability()
Does the gate work on a donor it was not fitted to
apply_gate_strategy()
Apply a learned gating strategy to new cells

Gate export

A learned gate that stays in R cannot be sorted on. These write it out in the units the FCS file stores, as ISAC Gating-ML 2.0 and as a plain table of vertices.

write_gating_ml()
Write learned gating strategies as a Gating-ML 2.0 document
polygons_linear_table()
The same polygons as a plain table in linear units
polygon_to_linear()
Subdivide polygon edges and return them in linear units

Statistics

Every test below uses per-sample values, so the replicates are donors rather than cells.

abundance_measure()
Pick the best available abundance measure, and say what it means
stats_group_comparison()
Test each population's abundance between groups
stats_marker_state()
Sample-level differential-state test: population x marker x group
stats_subcluster_shifts()
Per (cluster, subcluster, marker, study): how far is this study from reference
clr_frequencies()
Zero-safe centred log-ratio of each sample's population composition
compositional_concordance()
Concordance between the raw-percentage test and the CLR test
stats_confounding()
Is a covariate confounded with cohort, and does it track the outcome?
stats_rank_ancova()
Rank ANCOVA: cohort effect after adjusting for covariates (EXPLORATORY)
stats_paired_comparison()
Paired / repeated-measures abundance test

Batch structure

Measure the batch effect first, then decide. Correction is opt-in and is refused when batch and study group overlap far enough that removing one removes the other.

lisi_score()
Local Inverse Simpson's Index of a label over a neighbourhood graph
batch_mixing_report()
Batch-mixing diagnostic with a permutation null and a confounding check
correct_batch()
Correct batch effects in the transformed marker matrix

Diagnostics

Questions about the data and the gating that the analysis itself cannot answer.

stats_threshold_drift()
Test each marker's per-sample threshold for a cohort difference
write_run_manifest()
Write the run manifest

Conformance across runs

The within-run check in thresholds_used.csv compares each sample against its peers and catches one bad tube. It cannot catch a cohort that moved as a whole, because the peer median moves with it. A baseline written from an accepted run is the fixed reference that can.

write_spec_baseline()
Write a conformance baseline from an accepted run
read_spec_baseline()
Read a conformance baseline
specification_conformance()
Test this run against a baseline
spec_fingerprint()
Canonical text form of a population specification

Figures

QC heatmap for –absolute-counts: one tile per sample x population
fig_batch_diagnostic()
Batch diagnostic figure: the embedding coloured by batch, plus the LISI distribution against its permutation null
fig_cohort_confusion()
Cohort composition heatmap ("confusion matrix")
fig_density_by_sample()
Per-sample (or per-group) density comparison over the shared embedding
fig_frequency_uncertainty()
Population frequencies with the uncertainty of the gate that produced them
fig_functional_markers()
Functional-marker positivity figure
fig_gate_strategy()
Draw a proposed gating strategy, one panel per gate
fig_gating_qc()
Per-gate QC figure: every applied gate shown per sample with its threshold
fig_group_comparison()
Grouped abundance figure: one panel per population, bar + SD + every sample
fig_marker_grid()
Marker-expression grid over the shared embedding
fig_marker_state()
Differential-state figure, drawn by the baseline's own comparison figure
fig_multigraph_overlay()
FlowJo-style Multigraph Overlay: every cluster x every marker, one peak per group
fig_population_frequencies()
Population frequency figure – one lettered panel per population
fig_population_marker_heatmap()
Population x marker phenotype heatmap
fig_population_ratios()
Population-ratio figure – same layout as fig_group_comparison(), one panel per ratio defined in the config's ratios: block
fig_recon_diagnostics()
Initial reconnaissance / QC diagnostic figure – run on EVERY batch
fig_threshold_drift()
Threshold-drift figure: per-sample cut for every marker, coloured by cohort
fig_umap_overview()
Population + sample + covariate colouring panel set
fig_umap_overview_by_group()
Combined + per-group UMAP small multiples
fig_uncertainty_budget()
Where each population's uncertainty comes from
fig_unsupervised_clusters()
Unsupervised-clustering figure: the embedding by cluster, next to the same embedding by gate label
theme_cyto()
Publication-oriented minimal theme WHY: consistent, legible defaults across every emitted figure; outward ticks and frameless legends read better in print than ggplot2 defaults.

Metadata and export

load_patient_table()

load_sample_map()

load_absolute_counts()
Load, normalize, parse and sample-match an –absolute-counts input
export_flowjo_fcs()
